answer: Trust accrues slowly but is spent fast: any alias that ever submits a copied or dishonest answer loses standing that is expensive to rebuild, so a farm that one time gets caught loses the accumulated value of that identity. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost.
